The runtime therefore maps the keys to the accepted nodes (cross-branch reuse of accepted declarations with identical type, as the parent split did for cbr_ci_const_vector_massOn). Each child is the only node with its lean_name, so nothing reserved by another active branch is touched. Not splitting would make one leaf re-prove inline the three arguments already kernel-checked (111 lines in the accepted child commits), on top of the assembly.

- testform_comp (step 1, used in step 2): ω∘η is a test form.
- cycle_slices (steps 5–6): (SL) with the zero representation of ∂X = 0, plus the ISP of X, gives for a.e. t a slice A_X of X by {g < t} with ∂A_X integer multiplicity, for every Lipschitz g.

subproblems.title: Admissibility and change of variables for the dilated pair (λ^{−m}η_*μ, ξ(a + λ·))
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, a ∈ ℝ^P (Euclid P) and λ > 0, and let η := dilation a λ, η(y) = −λ⁻¹a + λ⁻¹y = λ⁻¹(y − a). Let μ be a measure on ℝ^P (Borel σ-algebra) with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P. Let ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_m(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P m, the continuous linear functionals on m-covectors) be μ-a.e. strongly measurable with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| (|α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α) for μ-a.e. x and every m-covector α. Put μ₂ := ofReal(λ^{−m})·η_*μ (Lean: ENNReal.ofReal (lam⁻¹ ^ m) • Measure.map (dilation a lam) μ) and ξ₂(y) := ξ(a + λy). Then: (a) μ₂(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P; (b) ξ₂ is μ₂-a.e. strongly measurable; (c) for μ₂-a.e. y, |ξ(a + λy)(α)| ≤ |α| for every m-covector α; (d) for every set S ⊆ ℝ^P and every map ω : ℝ^P → Λ^m(ℝ^P) (a DifferentialForm; no regularity assumed), ∫_S ξ(a + λy)(ω(y)) dμ₂(y) = λ^{−m}·∫_{η⁻¹(S)} ξ(x)(ω(η(x))) dμ(x) (Bochner integrals).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (a : Euclid P) (lam : ℝ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P m), 0 < lam → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → μ K < ∞) → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ μ → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) m, |ξ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → (ENNReal.ofReal (lam⁻¹ ^ m) • Measure.map (dilation a lam) μ) K < ∞) ∧ AEStronglyMeasurable (fun y => ξ (a + lam • y)) (ENNReal.ofReal (lam⁻¹ ^ m) • Measure.map (dilation a lam) μ) ∧ (∀ᵐ y ∂(ENNReal.ofReal (lam⁻¹ ^ m) • Measure.map (dilation a lam) μ), ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) m, |ξ (a + lam • y) α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) ∧ ∀ (S : Set (Euclid P)) (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m), ∫ y in S, ξ (a + lam • y) (ω y) ∂(ENNReal.ofReal (lam⁻¹ ^ m) • Measure.map (dilation a lam) μ) = lam⁻¹ ^ m * ∫ x in dilation a lam ⁻¹' S, ξ x (ω (dilation a lam x)) ∂μ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note: this child is the comparator-accepted DAG declaration cbr_ci_dsp_pushforward_pair (node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.closure_and_boundary_rectifiability-a1.cycle_im-a1.dilation_isp-a1.pushforward_pair-a1, status accepted, candidate commit 40b97a081c8a6bd695fef31025894a636e445c66, isolated comparator passed), whose frozen Lean type is byte-identical to the type below; its proof is recorded here so the contract is self-contained.
Source: parent proof, steps 1, 3 and 7. These steps show that η is a homeomorphism and measurable equivalence, that (λ^{−n}η_*μ_X, ξ_X(a + λ·)) is admissible, and the change of variables for the restricted integrals. Here they are extracted for an arbitrary pair (μ, ξ) in degree m and an arbitrary set S and form ω.
Notation: η := dilation a λ, so η(y) = −(λ⁻¹a) + dilationCLM P λ (y) = −λ⁻¹a + λ⁻¹y; c := ENNReal.ofReal(λ^{−m}), where λ^{−m} means (λ⁻¹)^m; μ₂ := c·η_*μ; ξ₂(y) := ξ(a + λy).
1. η is a homeomorphism. Since λ > 0, λ⁻¹ ≠ 0. Let e be the homeomorphism y ↦ λ⁻¹y (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero λ⁻¹ _) followed by the translation z ↦ −λ⁻¹a + z (Homeomorph.addLeft (−(λ⁻¹a))). For every y, e(y) = −λ⁻¹a + λ⁻¹y = η(y): unfold dilation and dilationCLM, using (λ⁻¹ • id)(y) = λ⁻¹y. So e = η as functions (funext). Consequences: (i) η is a measurable embedding of ℝ^P with its Borel σ-algebra (Homeomorph.measurableEmbedding, transported along e = η); (ii) for every compact K, η⁻¹(K) = e⁻¹(K) is compact (Homeomorph.isCompact_preimage).
2. Inverse identity. For every x ∈ ℝ^P: a + λ·η(x) = a + λ(−λ⁻¹a + λ⁻¹x) = a − (λλ⁻¹)a + (λλ⁻¹)x = x, since λλ⁻¹ = 1 (simp with smul_add, smul_smul and λ ≠ 0). Hence ξ₂(η(x)) = ξ(x) for all x, i.e. ξ₂ ∘ η = ξ.
3. Proof of (a). Let K be compact. Since η is a measurable embedding, (η_*μ)(K) = μ(η⁻¹(K)) (MeasurableEmbedding.map_apply, valid for every set). So μ₂(K) = c·μ(η⁻¹(K)) (Measure.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul). By 1(ii), η⁻¹(K) is compact, so μ(η⁻¹(K)) < ∞ by hypothesis. Also c = ofReal(λ^{−m}) < ∞ (ENNReal.ofReal_lt_top). A product of two finite elements of [0, ∞] is finite (ENNReal.mul_lt_top), so μ₂(K) < ∞.
4. Proof of (b). For the measurable embedding η, a map G is η_*μ-a.e. strongly measurable iff G ∘ η is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (MeasurableEmbedding.aestronglyMeasurable_map_iff). For G := ξ₂, step 2 gives G ∘ η = ξ, which is μ-a.e. strongly measurable by hypothesis. So ξ₂ is η_*μ-a.e. strongly measurable. Multiplying the measure by the constant c preserves a.e. strong measurability (AEStronglyMeasurable.smul_measure), so ξ₂ is μ₂-a.e. strongly measurable.
5. Proof of (c). Let p(y) be the statement ∀α, |ξ(a + λy)(α)| ≤ |α|. For the measurable embedding η, (∀ᵐ y ∂η_*μ, p(y)) ⟺ (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, p(η(x))) (MeasurableEmbedding.ae_map_iff). By step 2, p(η(x)) is the statement ∀α, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α|, which holds for μ-a.e. x by hypothesis (filter_upwards, then rewrite with step 2). So p holds η_*μ-a.e. Every η_*μ-null set N is μ₂-null, because μ₂(N) = c·0 = 0. Hence p holds μ₂-a.e. (Measure.ae_smul_measure).
6. Proof of (d). Fix S ⊆ ℝ^P and ω : ℝ^P → Λ^m(ℝ^P), and let G(y) := ξ(a + λy)(ω(y)) ∈ ℝ.
(i) Restriction commutes with scalar multiples of measures: μ₂⌞S = c·((η_*μ)⌞S) (Measure.restrict_smul).
(ii) For every function F and every measure ν, ∫F d(c·ν) = c.toReal·∫F dν (integral_smul_measure). No integrability is needed: if F is not integrable, both sides are 0.
(iii) c.toReal = λ^{−m}, because λ^{−m} = (λ⁻¹)^m ≥ 0 (ENNReal.toReal_ofReal with positivity).
(iv) Change of variables along the measurable embedding η, valid for every function and every set with no integrability hypothesis: ∫_S G d(η_*μ) = ∫_{η⁻¹(S)} G(η(x)) dμ(x) (MeasurableEmbedding.setIntegral_map).
(v) By step 2, G(η(x)) = ξ(a + λη(x))(ω(η(x))) = ξ(x)(ω(η(x))).
Combining (i)–(v), with smul_eq_mul: ∫_S ξ(a + λy)(ω(y)) dμ₂(y) = λ^{−m}·∫_{η⁻¹(S)} ξ(x)(ω(η(x))) dμ(x). This is (d), and together with (a)–(c) it proves the theorem. ∎
proof_key_steps: η = dilation a λ coincides with the homeomorphism (y ↦ λ⁻¹y) followed by (z ↦ −λ⁻¹a + z), so η is a measurable embedding and preimages of compact sets are compact.
Inverse identity a + λη(x) = x, hence ξ(a + λ·) ∘ η = ξ.
(a): μ₂(K) = ofReal(λ^{−m})·μ(η⁻¹K) < ∞ by MeasurableEmbedding.map_apply and compactness of η⁻¹K.
(b), (c): transfer a.e. strong measurability and the a.e. bound through MeasurableEmbedding.aestronglyMeasurable_map_iff / ae_map_iff and the inverse identity, then through the scalar multiple.
(d): restrict_smul, integral_smul_measure, toReal(ofReal λ^{−m}) = λ^{−m}, MeasurableEmbedding.setIntegral_map and the inverse identity.

subproblems.title: Composition with a dilation preserves test forms on ℝ^P
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, a ∈ ℝ^P (Euclid P) and λ > 0, and let η := dilation a λ, η(y) = −λ⁻¹a + λ⁻¹y. For every test m-form φ on ℝ^P, there is a test m-form φ' on ℝ^P with φ'(y) = φ(η(y)) for every y ∈ ℝ^P. Here a test m-form on ℝ^P is an element of TestFormOn univ m: a C^∞ map ℝ^P → Λ^m(ℝ^P) with compact support.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (a : Euclid P) (lam : ℝ), 0 < lam → ∀ φ : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m, ∃ φ' : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m, ∀ y : Euclid P, (φ' : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) y = (φ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) (dilation a lam y)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note: this child is the comparator-accepted DAG declaration cbr_ci_dsp_testForm_comp_dilation (node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.closure_and_boundary_rectifiability-a1.cycle_im-a1.dilation_isp-a1.testform_comp-a1, status accepted, candidate commit e7e69ec54f3d6b2477c0ae8c9bd09ce9eee5b343, isolated comparator passed), whose frozen Lean type is byte-identical to the type below; its proof is recorded here so the contract is self-contained.
Source: parent proof, step 1 (for a test form ω, ω∘η is a test form: it is smooth and tsupport(ω∘η) = η⁻¹(tsupport ω) is compact), extracted for test m-forms on ℝ^P.
Notation: η := dilation a λ, η(y) = −(λ⁻¹a) + dilationCLM P λ (y) = −λ⁻¹a + λ⁻¹y.
1. Smoothness. η is the sum of the constant map y ↦ −λ⁻¹a and the continuous linear map dilationCLM P λ, so η is C^∞ (contDiff_const.add (dilationCLM P λ).contDiff). The test form φ is C^∞: φ ∈ TestFormOn univ m means IsTestForm φ ∧ tsupport φ ⊆ univ, where IsTestForm φ = (ContDiff ℝ ∞ φ) ∧ HasCompactSupport φ; so the smoothness is φ.property.1.1. A composite of C^∞ maps is C^∞ (ContDiff.comp), so y ↦ φ(η(y)) is C^∞. In Lean, give this as the proof term φ.property.1.1.comp (contDiff_const.add (dilationCLM P lam).contDiff) rather than stating the type, because ∞ in the contract scope denotes ENNReal's top.
2. Compact support. Since λ > 0, λ⁻¹ ≠ 0. Let e be the homeomorphism y ↦ λ⁻¹y (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero λ⁻¹ _) followed by z ↦ −λ⁻¹a + z (Homeomorph.addLeft (−(λ⁻¹a))). Then e(y) = −λ⁻¹a + λ⁻¹y = η(y) for all y, so e = η (funext; simp with dilation, dilationCLM). φ has compact support (φ.property.1.2). A compactly supported function composed with a homeomorphism has compact support (HasCompactSupport.comp_homeomorph: tsupport(φ ∘ e) = e⁻¹(tsupport φ), which is compact). Rewriting e = η, φ ∘ η has compact support.
3. Support condition. tsupport(φ ∘ η) ⊆ univ trivially (subset_univ).
4. Conclusion. By steps 1–3, the form y ↦ φ(η(y)) satisfies IsTestForm and the support condition. So it defines an element φ' := ⟨fun y => φ(η(y)), ⟨⟨step 1, step 2⟩, step 3⟩⟩ of TestFormOn univ m, and φ'(y) = φ(η(y)) for every y by definition (rfl). ∎
proof_key_steps: η = constant + dilationCLM is C^∞, so φ ∘ η is C^∞.
η coincides with a homeomorphism, so φ ∘ η has compact support (HasCompactSupport.comp_homeomorph).
tsupport ⊆ univ is trivial; package φ ∘ η as an element φ' of TestFormOn univ m, with φ'(y) = φ(η(y)) by definition.

subproblems.title: Integer multiplicity slice boundaries of a cycle with the integer slice property
subproblems.statement:
Assume (SL), the exact frozen statement of the DAG theorem dimred_mbl_slice_mass_bounds (byte-identical to the frozen statement of cmc_slice_mass_bounds), which appears verbatim (parenthesized) as the first hypothesis of the Lean statement. (SL) says: let P, k ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U), and let μ, μ' be measures finite on compact subsets of U. Let ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_{k+1}(ℝ^P) and ξ' : ℝ^P → Λ_k(ℝ^P) be a.e. strongly measurable (for μ, resp. μ') with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| μ-a.e. and |ξ'(x)(α)| ≤ |α| μ'-a.e., with T(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ and ∂T(η) = ∫ξ'(η)dμ' for all test forms on U. Then for every L-Lipschitz f : ℝ^P → ℝ there are A_t ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U), B_t ∈ 𝒟_k(U) (t ∈ ℝ) with A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ and B_t(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ'(η)dμ'. Moreover ∂A_t(η) = B_t(η) whenever tsupport η is disjoint from {f = t}, and for open W, M_W(∂A_t − B_t) ≤ L·liminf_{h↓0}h⁻¹μ(W ∩ {t−h < f < t}) and ∫_a^b M_W(∂A_t − B_t)dt ≤ Lμ(W ∩ {a < f < b}).
Now let P, d ∈ ℕ and X ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) with ∂X = 0. Let μX be a measure on ℝ^P with μX(K) < ∞ for every compact K. Let ξX : ℝ^P → Λ_{d+1}(ℝ^P) be μX-a.e. strongly measurable with |ξX(x)(α)| ≤ |α| (|α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α) for μX-a.e. x and every α, and with X(ω) = ∫ξX(x)(ω(x))dμX(x) for every test (d+1)-form ω on ℝ^P. Reuse note: this child is the comparator-accepted DAG declaration cbr_ci_dsp_cycle_slice_boundary_im (node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.closure_and_boundary_rectifiability-a1.cycle_im-a1.dilation_isp-a1.cycle_slices-a1, status accepted, candidate commit b7f786d456d74a6ac75f8c6b4042b122362a6006, isolated comparator passed), whose frozen Lean type is byte-identical to the type below; its proof is recorded here so the contract is self-contained.
Source: parent proof, steps 5 and 6 (slices of the cycle X via (SL) with the zero representation of ∂X, and the ISP of X), with an arbitrary Lipschitz g in place of f∘η.
Fix L ≥ 0 and an L-Lipschitz g : ℝ^P → ℝ.
1. The zero pair represents ∂X admissibly. Let 0_μ be the zero measure on ℝ^P and 0_ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_d(ℝ^P) the zero map.
(i) 0_μ(K) = 0 < ∞ for every K (simp).
(ii) 0_ξ is 0_μ-a.e. strongly measurable: every function is a.e. strongly measurable for the zero measure (aestronglyMeasurable_zero_measure).
(iii) ∀ᵐ x ∂0_μ, ∀α, |0_ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α|. This holds because the zero measure's a.e. filter is trivial (simp); also |0| = 0 ≤ |α| pointwise.
(iv) For every test d-form η on ℝ^P: ∂X(η) = 0, since ∂X = 0 and the zero current evaluates to 0 (GeometricCurrentOn.zero_apply). Also ∫0_ξ(x)(η(x)) d0_μ(x) = 0 (integral_zero_measure). So ∂X(η) = ∫0_ξ(η) d0_μ (rw [hX]; simp).
2. Slices from (SL). Apply (SL) with U := ℝ^P (isOpen_univ), k := d, T := X, (μ, ξ) := (μX, ξX), (μ', ξ') := (0_μ, 0_ξ), f := g and Lipschitz constant L. The hypotheses are:
- compact-finiteness of μX on compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, i.e. the hypothesis on μX with the clause K ⊆ univ ignored;
- compact-finiteness of 0_μ (step 1(i));
- a.e. strong measurability of ξX (hypothesis) and of 0_ξ (step 1(ii));
- the a.e. bounds (hypothesis; step 1(iii));
- the representation X(ω) = ∫ξX(ω)dμX (hypothesis);
- the representation of ∂X by (0_μ, 0_ξ) (step 1(iv));
- LipschitzWith L g.
(SL) yields families A(t) ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P), B(t) ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P), t ∈ ℝ, with A(t)(ω) = ∫_{{g<t}} ξX(x)(ω(x)) dμX(x) and B(t)(η) = ∫_{{g<t}} 0_ξ(x)(η(x)) d0_μ(x) for all t, ω, η. The remaining three conclusions of (SL) are discarded.
3. Each B(t) is zero. For every t and η, B(t)(η) = ∫ 0_ξ(x)(η(x)) d(0_μ⌞{g<t}) = 0: the restriction of the zero measure is the zero measure (Measure.restrict_zero), the integral against it vanishes (integral_zero_measure), and the integrand is 0 anyway (simp). Since B(t) and the zero current agree on every test form, B(t) = 0 by extensionality of currents (GeometricCurrentOn.ext).
4. ISP of X. Apply the ISP hypothesis of X with (μ, μ', ξ, ξ') := (μX, 0_μ, ξX, 0_ξ), using the facts listed in step 2 (here compact-finiteness has no K ⊆ U clause: it is exactly the hypothesis on μX and step 1(i)), and with f := g, L and LipschitzWith L g. It yields: for L¹-a.e. t, every A₁ ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) and B₁ ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) with A₁(ω) = ∫_{{g<t}}ξX(ω)dμX for all ω and B₁(η) = ∫_{{g<t}}0_ξ(η)d0_μ for all η have ∂A₁ − B₁ integer multiplicity. It therefore suffices to prove the existence claim for each t in this full-measure set (filter_upwards).
5. Fix such a t. By step 2, A₁ := A(t) and B₁ := B(t) satisfy the two integral identities, so ∂A(t) − B(t) is integer multiplicity.
6. ∂A(t) − B(t) = ∂A(t). For every test d-form η, (∂A(t) − B(t))(η) = ∂A(t)(η) − B(t)(η), because the difference of currents is evaluated pointwise (the contract's Sub instance on GeometricCurrentOn subtracts the underlying linear maps). By step 3 this equals ∂A(t)(η) − 0 = ∂A(t)(η). By extensionality, ∂A(t) − B(t) = ∂A(t). Hence ∂A(t) is integer multiplicity (rewrite step 5 with this equality).
7. Conclusion. A := A(t) satisfies A(ω) = ∫_{{x : g(x) < t}} ξX(x)(ω(x)) dμX(x) for every test (d+1)-form ω (step 2), and ∂A is integer multiplicity (step 6). Since this holds for every t in the full-measure set of step 4, the conclusion holds for L¹-a.e. t. ∎
proof_key_steps: The zero measure with the zero field is an admissible representation of ∂X = 0.
(SL) applied to X with (μX, ξX), (0, 0) and g gives slice families A(t), B(t).
B(t) = 0 because it integrates against the zero measure; extensionality.
The ISP of X with the same data gives, for a.e. t, that ∂A(t) − B(t) is integer multiplicity.
∂A(t) − B(t) = ∂A(t) by extensionality, so A := A(t) witnesses the claim for a.e. t.
